title: Which blanks can we find in these two pyramids?
description: Two four row pyramids are filled by taking away at the end of a row and using a letter in a bottom blank. The first has forty in its second row and a third row ending in nine. The second has the top thirty five. Keeko doubts that the blank is twenty eight.
teaching_notes: One idea: start where a block at the end of a row has a known neighbour, then use one letter for the blank that sits under two blocks. Watch for students who take the known bottom numbers away from the block above and forget the blank is used twice.

video_script.why: A child fills two pyramids by taking away at the end of a row and using one letter for a blank under two blocks.
video_script.substitution: the book's own two pyramids, filled with take away and the letters pee and cue
video_script.anchor: two four row pyramids: the first with 40 in its second row, a third row ending in 9 and the bottom row 5, a blank, 7, a blank; the second with the top 35, a third row ending in 7 and the bottom row 3, 5 and two blanks
video_script.wrong_move: takes the two known bottom numbers away from the block above, forgetting that the bottom blank sits under both blocks and counts twice
video_script.payoff_line: The first pyramid has a bottom row of five, fourteen, seven and two, and a top of seventy.

final_answer.spoken: the first has a bottom row of five, fourteen, seven and two, and a top of seventy, and the second has a bottom row of three, five, five and two

maths_rules: First pyramid: the last bottom blank is 9 - 7 = 2.
Other bottom blank p: (5 + p) + (p + 7) = 40, so 12 + 2p = 40, 2p = 28, p = 14.
Third row 19, 21, 9; second row 40 and 21 + 9 = 30; top 40 + 30 = 70.
Second pyramid, bottom blank q after the 5: third row 8, 5 + q, 7; second row 13 + q and 12 + q; top 25 + 2q = 35, so q = 5.
Last bottom blank is 7 - 5 = 2; third row 8, 10, 7; second row 18 and 17; 18 + 17 = 35.
Doubt: 40 - 5 - 7 = 28 gives third row 33 and 35, which add to 68, not 40.
video_script.design: One idea: take away at the end of a row, then one letter for a blank under two blocks. The two pyramids stay in the anchor band and the first is finished before the second begins.
open_questions: The book prints these pyramids as figures that the text extract garbles; the numbers and blanks are placed as the worklist gives them.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.
<bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the blank is twenty eight, because forty take away five and seven leaves twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it. The third row becomes thirty three and thirty five, which make sixty eight.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That is not forty. The blank sits under both blocks, so it counts twice.
